column1: # Rescue verdicts: papers fermlit's first rubric EXCLUDED (or left borderline), re-screened
# under the second rubric in MTDNA_RUBRIC.md -- "does this paper help someone engineer the
# yeast mitochondrion or its genome?" -- extended to cover the Ehrlich/BCAA payload,
# compartment-specific cofactor measurement, protein targeting, genetic-code and codon
# engineering, and yeast genome-engineering methods that transfer.
# ONLY RESCUES ARE LISTED. A paper the second rubric also excluded stays excluded and has no
# row here; the file's job is to name what the first question threw away. Every row is a
# CHANGE from that paper's first-rubric verdict.
# The organism clause is deliberately opposite to the first rubric's instinct: a mammalian or
# plant mtDNA paper is included when the METHOD transfers, because those are often the only
# Re-screened: 2834 fermdb publications. Rescued to include: 709. To borderline: 549.
# TWO MODELS screened this corpus, and `decided_by` says per row which one decided that row.
# The run began on qwen3.6:27b -- the same local model that produced every first-rubric
# verdict -- and was stopped part-way when the GPU was needed elsewhere; the remainder ran on
# claude-sonnet-5 through the Claude Agent SDK. qwen rows: 348. sonnet rows: 910.
# The rubric, the two-pass structure and the 20-85 escalation band are identical across both
# halves; only the backend differs. Read `decided_by` before treating the file as homogeneous.
# Two passes, fermlit's own: title score, then abstract for the band (20-85).
# NOT INSTALLED -- installing is a curator act.
